newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up despite US dollar strength.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up despite US dollar strength.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar reversed an early slide to close slightly higher against the U.S. dollar on Thursday despite the U.S. currency's bold morning rise against the yen in Japan, dealers said.
The Taiwan dollar ended at T$27.498 to the U.S. dollar against Tuesday's T$27.499 close and well recovered from an early slip to T$27.505.
Turnover through dealers was a modest US$185 million. The market was closed on Wednesday for holiday.
Dealers said year-end demand for the U.S. dollar had not been as strong as expected.

"Foreign banks tried to push the Taiwan dollar down in response to the overseas trend," said one dealer. "But expected year-end U.S. dollar demand, which probably has neared its end, did not emerge to follow the foreign banks' move," she said.
On the contrary, the dealer said, exporters entered to supply U.S. dollars.
"Seeing that the Taiwan dollar is having difficulty to launch major movements, exporters have becoming quite willing to sell U.S. dollars around the T$27.50 level," she said.
For Friday, a stable T$27.495-27.505 range was seen.
